# Provenance and licences

The product is GPL-3.0-or-later. Original game data is neither relicensed nor included in packages.

* `src/saga2/`: SAGA2 from ScummVM revision `1a3e816afd5ddc41cc2a5c51a5da292e6d61758c`, GPL-3.0-or-later. Copyright notices remain in every imported file; see `SCUMMVM-COPYRIGHT` and the root `LICENSE`. [Source](https://github.com/scummvm/scummvm/tree/1a3e816afd5ddc41cc2a5c51a5da292e6d61758c/engines/saga2).
* `src/audio/midiparser.{h,cpp}`, `midiparser_xmidi.cpp`, `miles_adlib.cpp`: selected portable MIDI algorithms from that same ScummVM revision, GPL-3.0-or-later. `midi.h` provides a new one-source native interface, with MIDI constants from upstream `audio/mididrv.h` and Miles constants from `audio/miles.h`.
* `src/audio/nuked.{h,cpp}`, `nuked_wf_rom.h`: Nuked-OPL3-fast 1.8-fast.2 as distributed in that revision, LGPL-2.1-or-later, Nuke.YKT and Tony Gies. See `NUKED-LGPL-2.1`; original notices are retained. Only the chip algorithms remain; the ScummVM audio-chip adapter was removed.
* SDL 3.4.18: zlib licence, `SDL-LICENSE.txt`. Fetched as a checksum-pinned release archive, or provided by the builder. Bundled as a shared runtime library.
* `assets/fta2.png` and `assets/fta2.ico`: the ScummVM community game icon and its converted Windows sizes. See `APP-ICON.md` for pinned source, contributors, checksums and the supplied upstream GPL version 2 text. The icon is bundled explicitly; it is not verified as the original Windows release icon.
* The Windows cross-build uses Zig 0.16.0 and its statically linked C++/compiler runtimes. Notices for libc++, libc++abi and libunwind (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions), MinGW-w64 (its supplied COPYING notice), and Zig compiler runtime code (MIT) are preserved in `windows-runtime/`. These build-runtime components are separate from the imported SAGA2 code.

## Changes to imported code

Optional widescreen rendering adds a native display layout to the imported SAGA2 renderer and UI: a 654 × 420 map inside an 854 × 480 framebuffer, with the original sidebar translated by 214 pixels. The original 640 × 480 mode and 100-object rendering limit remain the defaults; wide mode allows 150 display objects without changing simulation activation distances. Options adds a persisted checkbox and defers buffer replacement until modal input and saved-background restoration finish. Modal centering, window clipping, camera offsets, speech placement and input bounds follow the active layout. Original decorative resources are reused without modifying game data, and gameplay save chunks remain unchanged.

Framework includes and `Common::` utility types were replaced by `platform/runtime.h` and `Native::` types backed by the C++ standard library. The native engine has no ScummVM `Engine`, `OSystem`, plugin registration, launcher, GUI debugger, configuration, stream, save manager or event infrastructure. Detection/metaengine/console implementation files are excluded from this product entirely. Gameplay, SAGA bytecode interpretation and software rendering remain in SAGA2.

DOS executable resources use the independently recovered DOS addresses and checked F2R1 pack. Unusable voice data is excluded, subtitles are mandatory, and missing movies finish immediately. Save files retain the original chunks, adding optional native RNG state. Reverse list traversal uses standard reverse iterators; closing the last window handles an empty list. The XMIDI/Miles algorithms use the native mixer and Nuked chip; MIDI timer callbacks are driven by generated audio samples. See `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/validation.md` for scope and verified limits.

`upstream-files.json` records SHA-256 hashes of the pristine imported source files, before these changes, to make the source revision and subsequent modifications auditable. The separate reference patches apply to the unmodified ScummVM revision; they are not linked into the product.

Native ownership fixes release retired motion tasks after the game step, detach cancelled path requests, and free player wrappers, association streams, effect prototype arrays, old band lists and the framebuffer. Motion tasks are value-initialized so save files do not contain uninitialized fields. These changes were checked against the reference world chunks and with AddressSanitizer/LeakSanitizer.

Version 0.1.6 extends the imported Options dialog with Hot Keys, reusing its original button images, decorative panels and fonts. The native shortcut overview has independent modal state and does not change gameplay bindings. The previously empty M handler now persists a music mute setting; the native music renderer applies it under its existing mutex while continuing sample-driven synthesis and XMIDI timing.

Version 0.1.7 reads both reserved IMPO import fields instead of discarding them; the first identifies the original credits script (110 in the supported DOS profile). The document renderer no longer prepends the obsolete imported W95 build stamp. Nested modal windows restore their parent modal pointer. Options uses visible ghosted artwork for mandatory speech text and an informational empty-save message without a restart action. Save discovery validates original save chunks, and header names are bounded before use.

Version 0.1.8 restores the imported Speech Text toggle and loads the persisted subtitles preference instead of forcing it on. Missing, empty or muted voice requests return failure before queueing, allowing the original text/timing fallback to operate. Saved speech voice flags are cleared before layout when voice playback is disabled. Completed speech tasks release their allocation after unlinking; the new dialogue scenario exposed the upstream disposal leak under LeakSanitizer. The supported data profile remains unchanged.

Document page-break removal copies the terminating null byte with the remaining text, preventing stale characters from appearing after the final credits paragraph. Original script text and page breaks are preserved.

Version 0.1.9 centralizes document cursor selection across opening, movement, dragging and release, excluding the close control. Document close and destruction restore the original normal pointer and hotspot. The native cursor adapter uploads pixels on every image update: address and size equality cannot establish unchanged content when composed cursor bitmaps are rebuilt. Existing book pagination and vertical document navigation are preserved.

Version 0.1.10 carries SDL wheel position and normalized vertical deltas through the internal native event path. The UI dispatcher delivers wheel events only to the top modal document without changing button or focus state. Vertical documents accumulate fractional movement privately and use the existing page-up/page-down handlers; their close controls and horizontal books remain outside wheel navigation. No game data or page artwork is changed.

Version 0.1.11 gives Escape priority to the frontmost open container during gameplay. It reuses the existing close-button callback, including original object scripts, open flags and deferred window cleanup. Modal dialogs retain their own Escape handling; O continues to open Options. The Hot Keys description now reflects container closure. No public API, option or game-data change is introduced.

Version 0.1.12 adds G/Shift+G to the imported gameplay key handler and a fourteenth row to Hot Keys, using 13-pixel row spacing within the existing 487 × 320 dialog. It searches the selected brother's carried objects with `RecursiveContainerIterator` and reuses `MotionTask::useObject`; Ctrl/Alt, UI locks, modal input, choice dialogue and object manipulation block it. Map identification comes from the immutable supported DOS `FTA.HRS` (SHA-256 `1d4fc56861bdc3f0e1dda1a21f48991e350dd8213fb694484f0f7fa731c7055d`), resource `LIST/PRO\0` at byte 17890, 52-byte record 320 at byte 34530: class 13 (Inventory), script 1149, name index 617. Original `LIST/OBJE` map objects 408, 3314 and 3315 are in Sacks 3887, 3888 and 3889. The unused `AutoMapProto` class and displayed names are not used for detection. No original data, public API, preference or CLI option changes.

Version 0.1.14 aligns the Widescreen checkbox with Night and Auto-Wield Weapon, reuses the original 18 × 17 checkbox bounds for hit testing and full redraw, and restores the 263-pixel Options height. It retains the original checkbox artwork and setting behavior.

Version 0.1.15 updates native SDL window sizing and development probes. The original per-world exploration algorithm, radius, corner exclusion and save format remain unchanged.

Version 0.1.16 removes duplicate control rectangles from the imported compressed-button classes and their constructor initialization. Hit testing, rendering and state-change invalidation now share the inherited panel bounds after widescreen translation. The original artwork and gameplay selection rules are preserved.
